column1: # Member inventory for the client binary: fields, consts, events,
# properties and enum members, each owned by the type that DECLARES
# it. Members of a nested type belong to the nested type, not to its
# parent; that distinction is what makes a struct projection correct
# (dec018), and it is why the counts here reconcile exactly with the
# field_type is the declared C# type, verbatim, including generics and
# array suffixes; the projection maps it, it is not rewritten here.
# `value` is the initializer of a const or an enum member, verbatim, and
# only when it is a simple literal; '-' otherwise. A string constant's
# value is stored WITHOUT its surrounding quotes, because a quoted cell
# is a token/merge hazard in the canonical form and the type is already
# declared `string`. Without this column the 14,880 constants here would
# project as names with no data.
# `ord` is the declaration order within the type, which the sheet's id
# sort would otherwise lose. A Rust struct's fields are projected in it,
# and an enum member with no explicit value takes the next index.
# A field and a nested type can fold to the same id (see the types sheet,
# dropped_reason: lines inside a type body that are not member declarations (braces, get/set accessors, and statements that belong to an initializer)
